  - text: CLASS 9 · EUCLIDEAN GEOMETRY
  - heading "Euclid's Five Postulates" [level=1]
  - paragraph: Foundational assumptions of Euclidean geometry. Use the explorer to visualize and understand each postulate.
  - text: "30 min Interact Level: Foundation Grade: 9 Euclidean Geometry"
  - img "Parchment with Euclidean constructions and a compass"
  - navigation:
    - button "Interact"
    - button "Learn"
    - button "Example"
    - button "Formula"
    - button "Practice"
  - main:
    - heading "Explore the Five Postulates" [level=2]
    - paragraph: Select a postulate, then use the tools to see it in action. Feedback updates in real time.
    - button "Reset":
      - img
      - text: Reset
    - button "Fullscreen construction":
      - img
    - complementary:
      - button "1 Postulate 1 A straight line can be drawn from any one point to any other point."
      - button "2 Postulate 2 A terminated straight line can be produced indefinitely in a straight line."
      - button "3 Postulate 3 A circle can be drawn with any centre and any radius."
      - button "4 Postulate 4 All right angles are equal to one another."
      - button "5 Postulate 5 (Parallel) If a straight line falling on two straight lines makes the interior angles on the same side less than two right angles, the lines meet on that side."
    - article:
      - navigation:
        - button "╱ Select"
        - button "● Point"
        - button "╱ Line"
        - button "╱ Extend"
        - button "○ Circle"
        - button "△ Angle"
        - button "⌁ Measure"
      - img "Interactive Euclidean construction": A B
      - img
      - text: "Well done! A straight line has been drawn from A to B. Postulate 1: A straight line can be drawn from any one point to any other point."
      - paragraph: You chose two distinct points A and B. A unique straight line AB has been drawn.
      - paragraph:
        - strong: "Tip:"
        - text: Drag the points or choose a tool to explore the construction.
    - article:
      - heading "Why it works" [level=2]:
        - img
        - text: Why it works
      - paragraph: These postulates are basic assumptions about points, lines, and planes. They are not proved, but accepted as true because geometry depends on them.
      - paragraph: ✓ They form the foundation.
      - paragraph: ✓ All theorems are built on them.
      - paragraph: ✓ Postulate 5 is the most subtle.
    - article:
      - heading "Worked Example (Postulate 3)" [level=2]
      - paragraph: A circle can be drawn with any centre and radius.
      - img: O P 5 cm
      - paragraph: "Construction: 1. Mark point O as centre. 2. Set radius OP = 5 cm. 3. With O as centre and radius 5 cm, draw a circle."
      - text: "Result: Circle with centre O and radius 5 cm is drawn."
    - article:
      - heading "Common Misconception" [level=2]:
        - img
        - text: Common Misconception
      - paragraph: Postulate 5 does not say “parallel lines never meet.” It is a conditional statement.
      - img: 60° 70°
      - paragraph: Since 60° + 70° = 130° < 180°, the lines will meet on this side when produced indefinitely.

    - paragraph: Match each geometric action to the correct postulate.
